summary.headline: Gopal Snacks Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR 422.3 cr (+31.1% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 7.4%; FY27 EBITDA guided at 8-9%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered record quarterly revenue from operations of INR 422.3 crore, up 31.1% YoY and 3.1% QoQ, with the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential growth. EBITDA more than doubled YoY to INR 31.5 crore (7.4% margin vs 4.7%), and PAT was INR 12.8 crore. Rajkot main facility restarted after the Gondal consolidation, though April saw about 5-6 working days of disruption (gas shortage and plant shift) that cost INR 12-13 crore of revenue in core markets. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20%+ growth (INR 1,800-1,900 crore revenue) and 8-9% EBITDA margin with exit near double digits.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 5.3 crore in Q1 FY26
No exceptional items in Q1; prior quarter had insurance gain, so QoQ not comparable
May and June at this level

segments.name: Core market (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Flat sequentially in Q1 due to April disruption that cost INR 12-13 crore; management targets INR 100-plus crore per month from here. Gathiya is the leading product, followed by namkeen, snack pellets and potato wafers; wafers grew 15% YoY in core markets. About 65% of Gujarat Gathiya market is still unorganised.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 41% YoY; 100% of UP top line comes from two SKUs, Champakali Gathiya and Papdi Gathiya.

segments.name: Focus and other states
segments.commentary: Focus-state distributors rose from 440 (Q1 FY26) to 530 (Q4 FY26) to 567 (Q1 FY27); other states rose from 110 to 129. Maharashtra distributors went 194 to 205 to 198, with focus on Marathwada and the Nagpur belt.

segments.name: Other snack products
segments.commentary: Revenue in the other snacks bucket went from about INR 10 crore last year to about INR 23-24 crore per quarter, including Shot Go noodles, rusks, wafer biscuits, wafer rolls, jeera biscuits and washing bar.

segments.name: Alternate channels
segments.commentary: E-commerce was INR 2.79 crore in Q1 FY27 vs INR 2 crore in Q4 FY26. Modern trade was flat at INR 1.85 crore.

segments.name: Nagpur plant
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation is below 30%; 159 distributors were mapped to Nagpur, of which about 60 have moved to Modasa for logistics reasons. Third-party units at Kashipur (about INR 2 crore per month) and Manendragarh support other regions.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR 1,800-1,900 crore (20%+ growth), reaffirmed; management says it has held the stance on 20%+ growth.
FY27 EBITDA margin 8-9% for the full year, with exit run rate near double digits.
FY28 EBITDA margin guided at 10-11% with exit near 11%; sustainable target 11-11.5%; average reaching that level around mid-FY28-29.
FY28 PAT margin around 7-7.5%; minimum 20% revenue CAGR over the medium term.
Insurance claim of about INR 30-40 crore on the fire loss expected in Q2 FY27; management says documents are submitted.
Seven NPIs planned across Q2 and Q3, five of them non-palm-oil with better margins; 6 lakh outlets targeted by end of CY2026 (from 5.25-5.5 lakh).
capex_capacity: Rajkot main facility restarted; production consolidated from Gondal to Rajkot, with expected savings in power, fuel, logistics and operating costs as utilisation improves.
Modasa and Nagpur plants contribute to the network; Nagpur utilisation is below 30%.
Double-service coverage now reaches 38% of outlets; run rate up 14-25% where it has been rolled out. Pilot of ARS (auto replenishment) started; DMS covers most of the distributor network.
Retail touchpoints on DMS at 4.24 lakh; another 60-70k outlets are served but not on DMS.
demand_pricing: Raw material inflation was 5% in Q1; 4.2% passed on through price hikes and grammage cuts, 0.8% absorbed in P&L. Another 0.2-0.3% hit is pending and will be passed through.
Q2 inflation is slightly lower than 100 bps additional, per management.
Management says the company now runs at par or lower grammage than competitors and relies on distribution automation rather than grammage to drive volume.
Management expects roughly 75-80% of growth from volume and about 20% from price in the rest of FY27.
Chana stored till Q3-end; potato stored; palm oil and laminate are bought from the market with no major near-term increase foreseen.
INR 5 price point remains about 60% of sales (down from ~80% in FY22); management says no visible industry shift.
Regional brands in core states (Balaji, Gokul, Shri Hari) remain present; Miraj and Star brands shut, and Miraj has restarted.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 330-350 crore FY27 incremental revenue guidance still intact, and what is the festive run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the run rate is INR 150 crore+ per month, April was lower due to the Gondal to Rajkot shift, and 20%+ growth guidance stands.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin and when will it ramp up?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable target is 11-11.5%. FY27 exit near double digits, FY28 exit near 11%, and an average of that level around mid-FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core market run rate target and how is the Gujarat business growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of INR 100-plus crore per month in core markets. Double service is being scaled up, and more products are planned to lift margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the A&P and trade spend trends?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P was about 1% of sales in Q1 against a 2.2% annualised budget; trade discount is 2.5% of sales versus about 3.5% earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Nagpur utilisation below 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: 159 distributors were mapped to Nagpur, about 60 were moved to Modasa for logistics, and the 250-distributor-a-year addition is below plan for the 300-400 km catchment.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an FMCG business with no order book, and daily run rate is steady with no month-end billing.
